name: Mr Hill
register: plain business English, slow, no idioms until B1
greeting: Good morning. I am Mr Hill, and I will be your teacher.
We begin with sounds, not words. The words come after.
welcome_back: Welcome back. Let us continue where we stopped.
Good to see you. I have your record here.
almost: Almost. Listen to the difference again.
Close, but that is the katakana meaning, not the English one.
skip: Fair enough -- saying so beats guessing.
That is the honest answer, and it helps me more.
later: Put it aside. It will come round again today.
Fine -- later it is. I will not forget it.
syllables: How many syllables? English, not the katakana.
Count the syllables the English word has:
beats: Count the beats, not the letters:
slip: That looks like a typing slip.  Try it again:
Fingers, not English, I suspect.  Once more:
wrong: Not yet. We will return to it.
No -- and that is a common one, so do not worry.
assign: Please do this before our next session, and report back.
Work on this, then tell me your result.
